title: For AI agents: set up pi-durable-bot (Pots)
description: For AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) that set up pi-durable-bot (Pots) for a person: the steps, the commands, and the one step that is theirs.
claim: You install Pots and make the bot. Your person signs in to a model. The bot then connects its own chat apps.

steps.title: Warn your person first
steps.text: The bot gets full control of the computer it runs on, with no approval step. Recommend a computer or VM of its own; go on only if they agree.

steps.title: Install where the bot will live
steps.text: Node.js 24 or newer, on macOS, Linux or Windows. Over SSH, run it on the server.

steps.title: See what it can use
steps.text: Lists the models and judges ready on this computer, never a secret.

steps.title: Ask only what is missing
steps.text: Its name, what it is for, how it gets its AI, and who decides on group messages: the bot or Jev.

steps.title: Your person signs in
steps.text: If their choice is not listed, they run this in their own terminal; keys never pass through your chat.

steps.title: Make the bot
steps.text: Pick the newest strong model listed and say which. `--yes` accepts step 1. `--judge off` if no group chats; `--judge typesafe/jev-latest` for Jev.
steps.code: pots init --yes --name "Ada" --model openai/gpt-6.1-sol --about "our team's research and ops assistant" --no-chat

steps.title: Check, then hand over
steps.text: It must print the bot's answer. Then your person runs `pots chat` to meet the bot.

rules: Do not create the chat app, collect tokens or edit `~/.pots/` by hand. The bot does that itself.
Run `pots mcp add` only when your person asks for an MCP server.
